title: My Amazing Body
subtitle: Heart, lungs, bones and the germs they fight
subject: Body

p: You have one body. It is all yours.
It works all day. It works all night, even when you sleep.
Wiggle your toes. Your body did that!

v.title: Every body is different. Every body is amazing.

pages.cap: Big or small, every body is busy inside.

p: Make a fist. That is how big your heart is.
It sits in your chest. It squeezes and squeezes.
Every squeeze pushes blood all around your body.
pages.cap: Blood goes in, the heart squeezes, blood goes out.
pages.fact: Did you know? Your heart beats more than 100,000 times every day.

p: You need just your hand.
steps: Put your hand flat on the left side of your chest. Feel the thump?
Now jump up and down ten times.
Feel again. Faster? Your heart is working harder.
pages.cap: Your heart speeds up when you move.
pages.safe: Stop and rest if you feel dizzy.

p: When you sit still, your heart beats about 100 times a minute.
When you run, it goes faster. Much faster!
When you sleep, it slows right down.
pages.cap: Count the beats in one minute. How many did you get?

pages.q: What does your heart push around your body?
pages.why: The heart is a pump. It pushes blood through tubes to every part of you.

p: Take a big breath. Feel your chest grow?
Inside are two lungs. They fill up like balloons.
Air goes in through your nose. Down, down into your lungs.
pages.cap: Breathe in and your lungs get big.

p: Now blow on your hand. Warm, right?
That air came from deep inside you.
Your body warmed it up. Then your lungs pushed it out.
pages.cap: Breathe out and your lungs get small again.

pages.h: You breathe about 20 times every minute.
p: Even while you sleep. Even while you read this. You never have to remember to do it. Your body just knows.
Inside you is a frame made of bones.
A grown-up has 206 bones. A baby has about 300! Some join together as you grow.
Bones hold you up, like poles in a tent.
pages.cap: All your bones together are called a skeleton.
pages.fact: Did you know? The smallest bone is in your ear. It is smaller than a grain of rice.

p: Knock gently on your head. Hard! That is your skull.
Press your knee. Press your elbow.
Those hard bits are bones. They keep the soft bits safe.
pages.cap: Your skull is a helmet for your brain.

pages.why: Bones are hard and strong. They are the frame that holds you up.

p: Bend your arm. Feel the bump? That is a muscle.
Muscles pull on your bones to move them.
Your arm works like a seesaw. The muscle pulls and your hand lifts.
pages.cap: A small pull from a muscle lifts your whole arm.
pages.fact: Did you know? You have more than 600 muscles.

p: Skin covers you from head to toe.
It keeps the wet in and the germs out.
It can feel hot, cold, soft and tickly. Tickle your own arm!
pages.cap: Your skin is made of millions of tiny cells.

p: Your brain is the boss of everything.
It tells your legs to run. It tells your mouth to smile.
It sends messages along thin threads called nerves.
pages.cap: A message jumps from one nerve cell to the next.

pages.h: A message from your brain to your toe takes less than a blink.
p: Think about wiggling your big toe. Now do it. See how fast that was?
Germs are tiny living things. Too tiny to see!
They are on door handles, on toys, on your hands.
Most are harmless. Some can make you sick.
pages.cap: Germs are so small that thousands fit on one fingertip.

p: Germs get in? Your body fights back!
White blood cells hunt the germs and gobble them up.
A fever means your army is busy. Rest helps it win.
pages.cap: A white blood cell catches a germ.

pages.h: Try it: wash like a pro
p: You need soap, water and a sink.
steps: Rub! Front, back, between the fingers, under the nails.
Count slowly to 20. Then rinse and dry.
pages.cap: Soap and rubbing wash the germs away.
pages.safe: Check the water is warm, not hot.

pages.q: How long should you rub your hands with soap?
pages.why: Twenty seconds of rubbing gives the soap time to lift the germs off.

p: A sneeze shoots germs into the air. Fast!
Catch it in your elbow, not your hand.
Then your hands stay clean for playing.
pages.cap: A sneeze is loud and fast. Cover it with your elbow.

p: At night your body fixes itself.
It grows. It heals cuts. It fights germs.
You need about 10 to 13 hours of sleep. That is a lot of fixing!
pages.cap: While you sleep, your body is hard at work.

p: You grow about 6 centimetres every year.
That is about the length of your finger.
Mark your height on a wall. Check again next year!

v.title: Look how much you have grown!

pages.cap: A new baby is about 50 centimetres long. You are twice that now.

items: the pump that pushes blood around you
two bags in your chest that fill with air
the hard parts that hold you up
a part that pulls bones to move you
a tiny living thing that can make you sick

qs: What is the most amazing thing your body can do?
Which germs do you think live on your favourite toy? How could you get rid of them?
If you could ask your heart one question, what would it be?
